name: xQc (Félix Lengyel)
role: Canadian Twitch streamer and content creator (born 1995)
summary: A gaming streamer with no political record beyond taking political quizzes on stream. Across those runs he is pro-universal healthcare, public utilities and abortion rights, supports same-sex marriage, and is against worker ownership, gun limits and drug legalization; he wants regulation of monopolies and corporations but is sceptical of government-funded media and of equal distribution by need.

universal-healthcare.rationale: In the 8Values run he strongly agreed with single-payer universal healthcare, defending Canada's system (with a parallel private sector allowed); in the Compass runs he praised Quebec's health card over US billing.

public-ownership.rationale: 8Values: strongly agreed that basic utilities like roads and electricity should be publicly owned, arguing private ownership would mean subscriptions for every stretch of road.

tax-the-wealthy.rationale: 8Values: only slightly agreed that taxes on the rich should rise, wanting everyone to pay more for public benefit rather than just for the poor; in both Compass runs he disagreed that the rich are too heavily taxed.

regulate-corporations.rationale: 8Values: strongly agreed that government must intervene to protect consumers; Compass: strongly agreed corporations cannot be trusted to protect the environment and said they 'have to be told what to do'. He never said how much more regulation.

worker-ownership.rationale: 8Values: 'absolutely not' to the means of production belonging to the workers who use them; he said paid operators do not own the machine and it would breed resentment.

surveillance-ok.rationale: 8Values (newest): agreed civil liberties may be sacrificed against terrorism and that government surveillance is necessary, accepting the trade-off; earlier Compass runs disagreed that only wrongdoers need worry, so not high.

legalize-drugs.rationale: 8Values: disagreed with legalizing or decriminalizing drug use ('full disagree', drugs equal bad). He agreed marijuana possession should not be criminal in the older Compass runs; the newer answer on drugs generally wins.

strong-leader.rationale: 8Values: agreed 'the stronger the leadership, the better' as a core concept; the item does not mention bypassing gridlock.

state-harmful.rationale: 8Values: disagreed the state is a threat to liberty and said a hierarchical state is fine, with anarchy or a king the only alternatives and both rejected.

limit-guns.rationale: 8Values: strongly disagreed that gun ownership should be prohibited for those without a valid reason; he called it a right and said to fix the illness, not the guns.

rehabilitation.rationale: Strongly disagreed in both Compass runs that punishment should matter more than rehabilitation (though he said a few are lost causes who must be locked away).

same-sex-marriage.rationale: 8Values: agreed same-sex marriage should be legal and said he does not care what people do; also agreed in the Compass runs that same-sex couples should be able to adopt.

abortion-legal.rationale: 8Values: strongly disagreed that abortion should be prohibited in most cases; in the second Compass run he said an unconscious, brain-dead state is not yet a life.

humanitarian-intervention.rationale: Compass runs: agreed military action defying international law is sometimes justified, citing someone doing extreme harm to everybody, and 8Values: sovereignty should yield to outside interference over human rights.

tariffs-protect-industry.rationale: 8Values: agreed tariffs on international trade are important to encourage local production; in the Compass runs he agreed protectionism is sometimes necessary against sweatshop-based competition.

one-party-rule.rationale: Disagreed (strongly in the first run) that one-party rule's avoidance of argument is an advantage, saying a state with no questioning goes brain dead.

military-superiority.rationale: 8Values: strongly disagreed that military spending is wasted, saying a country without force has no leverage and invites abuse, but also that wanting to dominate the world is bad.

restore-past-order.rationale: 8Values: disagreed that society was better many years ago, saying the overall path is improving, and agreed reason matters more than maintaining culture.

distribute-by-need.rationale: Rejected 'from each according to ability, to each according to need' in all three runs (strongly in both Compass runs, 'dumb' and 'a joke' in 8Values) because the human component makes it collapse.

avoid-deficit-stimulus.rationale: 8Values: strongly agreed a balanced budget beats welfare for all citizens, arguing a government borrowing trillions cannot sustain spending; this is a nearby but not identical item.

force-without-un.rationale: Same Compass item (strongly agreed in the second run): force that defies international law is sometimes justified, which covers acting without UN approval.

work-for-welfare.rationale: Strongly agreed in both Compass runs that people able to work who refuse opportunity should not expect society's support.

sacrifice-heritage.rationale: Disagreed in both Compass runs that taxpayers should not prop up theaters and museums that cannot pay their way, arguing forgetting history means losing who we are.

racial-segregation-law.rationale: Same Compass item as above, rejecting that different groups should be kept apart.

assimilate-immigrants.rationale: 8Values: only slightly agreed immigrants should integrate into the culture, not strongly, as locals are not held to that standard; he also thinks first-generation immigrants can fully integrate.

national-mission.rationale: 8Values: disagreed that our nation's values should be spread as much as possible, as nobody's culture is better and people should do their own thing.

heritable-defect-limits.rationale: Compass: first run slightly disagreed, second slightly agreed for very serious cases; 8Values called eugenics terrible, so the record points both ways.

discourage-race-mixing.rationale: Disagreed in both Compass runs that different sorts of people should keep to their own kind ('there is no kind, it's humankind').

equal-moral-worth.rationale: 8Values: strongly agreed all people, regardless of culture or sexuality, should be treated equally ('a no-brainer').

no-religion-state-schools.rationale: Strongly disagreed in both Compass runs, and in 8Values, that schools should instill religious values: those who care can do it at home.

pool-sovereignty.rationale: 8Values: agreed with regional unions such as the EU, reasoning from NAFTA-style trade and like-minded countries grouping together.

cultures-equal-different.rationale: Compass runs disagreed there are no savage and civilized peoples, only different cultures; 8Values he leaned to no culture being superior ('it's just different').

death-penalty.rationale: Both Compass runs: agreed the death penalty should be an option for the most serious crimes, case by case, noting prison costs everyone.

restrict-pornography.rationale: First Compass run: agreed that explicit depiction of consenting adults should be legal for adults, as a means of expression.

ban-cartels.rationale: Compass runs: agreed (strongly in the first) that a genuine free market needs restrictions on predatory multinationals forming monopolies, calling monopolies trash that crush competition.

non-intervention.rationale: 8Values: on national sovereignty he said sovereignty is good but the world should possibly interfere when a state abuses human rights (child labour, rejecting human rights).

local-production.rationale: His spoken reason for the tariffs item in 8Values was that producing and buying closer to home cuts pointless trade, saving fuel and time and giving fresher goods.

criminalize-homosexuality.rationale: His agreement that private bedroom conduct between consenting adults is not the state's business (Compass), same-sex marriage and adoption support cannot coexist with criminalising it.

assisted-dying.rationale: 8Values: agreed physician-assisted suicide should be legal in terminal cases, saying a person who can only communicate by heart rate should be allowed to have the plug pulled.

charity-over-state-aid.rationale: Strongly disagreed in both Compass runs that charity is better than social security, and in 8Values that social programs should be abolished for private charity: charity is the last line of defence and the government should do it.

public-service-media.rationale: Both Compass runs: agreed that no broadcaster, however independent, should get public funding, distrusting state-funded media and any claim of independence.

premarital-sex.rationale: Disagreed in both Compass runs that sex outside marriage is usually immoral, and said in 8Values he does not care about such tradition-based morality.

notes: Quiz runs that disagreed: marijuana possession (agree in Compass runs vs. drugs should stay illegal in 8Values: newest wins for legalize-drugs); surveillance (Compass runs sceptical, 8Values accepting); cultures-equal-different and heritable-defect-limits answered 0 low. Jokey or unclear answers skipped (prostitution, United Nations, national sovereignty polarity, shareholders-only responsibility which flipped between runs, violence against authoritarian regimes). Chat-read lines and the 2024 comparison/results videos gave no item-level answers. Web and local corpora searches found no other stated positions; Wikipedia states none.
